story.title: Trump, Xi, and Putin to Hold Historic Meeting at APEC Summit in China
story.summary: The leaders of the United States, China, and Russia are set to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China. This meeting marks the first formal gathering of the three leaders, with discussions expected to focus on nuclear weapons reduction. The meeting is scheduled for next week.

explore_lenses.label: Why are nuclear talks on the agenda now?
explore_lenses.title: New START’s lapse raised the stakes
explore_lenses.summary: The meeting follows the February 2026 expiration of New START, leaving no agreed limits on U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear arsenals. The Trump administration had already advocated bringing China into trilateral arms-control talks during Xi’s September visit to Washington.

claims.text: The United Nations says New START expired on February 5, 2026 without a successor arrangement, meaning that for the first time since the 1970s there are no agreed limits on U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear arsenals.
In a September 25 White House fact sheet on Xi’s U.S. visit, the administration said Trump advocated trilateral arms-control negotiations among the United States, Russia, and China.
AP reported that Trump rejected a Russian call to extend the former U.S.-Russia arrangement for another year and instead called for a replacement agreement including China.

points: The United Nations says New START expired on February 5, 2026 without a successor arrangement, meaning that for the first time since the 1970s there are no agreed limits on U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear arsenals.
In a September 25 White House fact sheet on Xi’s U.S. visit, the administration said Trump advocated trilateral arms-control negotiations among the United States, Russia, and China.
AP reported that Trump rejected a Russian call to extend the former U.S.-Russia arrangement for another year and instead called for a replacement agreement including China.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: No draft framework, negotiating mandate, or verification proposal for a successor arrangement has been publicly released.
explore_lenses.note: Researched context; forecasts and viewpoints are labeled and attributed.

explore_lenses.label: Why will a three-way arms deal be difficult?
explore_lenses.title: China rejects equal trilateral obligations
explore_lenses.summary: China’s stated position is that the United States and Russia, as the holders of much larger arsenals, must make major verifiable reductions before China joins multilateral disarmament negotiations. U.S. officials nevertheless describe the Shenzhen meeting as an opening conversation rather than a deal-making session.

claims.text: China’s Foreign Ministry said in April that it was not fair, reasonable, or realistic to ask China at this stage to join trilateral nuclear-disarmament negotiations, and said the states with the largest arsenals have a primary responsibility to reduce them substantially.

AP reported U.S. estimates of more than 5,000 warheads each for the United States and Russia, compared with a Pentagon estimate of more than 600 for China; the numerical imbalance helps explain Beijing’s position.
A senior U.S. official told AP that no agreement is expected at the meeting and characterized it as the beginning of a potentially productive arms-control conversation.

explore_lenses.label: What is confirmed for the Shenzhen meeting?
explore_lenses.title: A November 19 trilateral beside APEC
explore_lenses.summary: China has confirmed that the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting runs in Shenzhen on November 18–19. Reporting based on White House confirmation places the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting on November 19, with nuclear arms and the Iran war on the stated agenda.

claims.text: China’s Foreign Ministry announced that Xi will chair the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen on November 18–19, with a CEO summit scheduled for November 17–18.
RFE/RL reported that the White House confirmed a November 19 Trump-Xi-Putin meeting on the sidelines of APEC and said nuclear-arms reduction and the Iran war are expected topics.

According to RFE/RL’s account of U.S. officials’ briefing, Russia’s war against Ukraine is not expected to be explicitly discussed, and Trump and Putin are not scheduled to hold a separate bilateral meeting during the visit.

story_report.summary: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are set to meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, in what officials describe as the first formal trilateral gathering of the U.S., Chinese and Russian leaders. Nuclear-arms reductions are expected to be a central subject, alongside the Iran war. The meeting is expected to open a broader arms-control conversation rather than yield an agreement, according to a senior U.S. official.

sections.heading: Arms-Control Limits Have Lapsed
sections.body: The talks will take place after the expiration of New START on February 5, 2026, without a successor arrangement. The United Nations said the lapse left the United States and Russia without agreed limits on their strategic nuclear arsenals for the first time since the 1970s. The Trump administration had previously said Trump advocated trilateral arms-control negotiations involving Washington, Moscow and Beijing.

sections.heading: China Resists Trilateral Negotiations
sections.body: Beijing has argued that it is neither fair nor realistic for China to join trilateral nuclear-disarmament negotiations at this stage, saying the countries with the largest arsenals bear the primary responsibility for substantial reductions. AP reported U.S. estimates of more than 5,000 warheads each for the United States and Russia, compared with a Pentagon estimate of more than 600 for China. That disparity helps explain China’s position.

sections.heading: APEC Meeting Schedule and Agenda
sections.body: China’s Foreign Ministry said Xi will chair the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen on November 18-19, after a CEO summit scheduled for November 17-18. RFE/RL reported that the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting is planned for November 19. U.S. officials said Russia’s war against Ukraine is not expected to be explicitly discussed, and Trump and Putin are not scheduled to hold a separate bilateral meeting during the visit.

unresolved.text: No draft framework, negotiating mandate or verification proposal for a successor arms-control arrangement has been publicly released.
It remains unclear whether China would accept negotiations covering transparency, warhead limits, delivery systems or verification.
The governments have not publicly released a detailed meeting agenda, attendee list, duration, joint-statement plan or follow-up negotiating schedule.

related_stories.title: Nationwide Flight Ground Stop in the US Due to Equipment Overload
related_stories.summary: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration implemented a nationwide ground stop, resulting in over 8,200 flight cancellations, which accounted for more than 31% of scheduled flights in the US. The ground stop lasted nearly five hours, marking the longest such event since September 11, 2001. Officials attributed the disruption to outdated air traffic communications equipment and confirmed there was no evidence of a cyber attack. Flights have since resumed as airspace reopened.

related_stories.title: US Suggests Ukraine Consider Territorial Cession for NATO Membership, Says Zelenskyy
related_stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the United States has proposed the idea of Ukraine ceding parts of the Donbas region to Russia as a condition for joining NATO. This marks the first time the US has raised the possibility of territorial concessions in exchange for NATO membership. Zelenskyy indicated that discussions are ongoing regarding specific security guarantees from Western allies.
